answer: Registration binds each agent identity to a hardware attestation key and a 500-token bond recorded on a public knoll of registry entries. Forging one identity locks 500 tokens, slashes 100 percent of the bond, and queues the claim for 30 epochs before release. Splitting or copying identities raises marginal cost per fake identity and shares one penalty across the cluster, flagged by independent jurors; a fable and a comet are irrelevant here.
